children.h: 1 · Is the newborn sick or bleeding?

children.cond: High-pitched cry, arching, abnormal tone or poor suck in a deeply jaundiced infant

pill.text: Emergency department now: possible bilirubin encephalopathy — total and direct bilirubin and albumin now; intensive phototherapy now; neonatal team for urgent exchange transfusion; sepsis evaluation

children.cond: Poor feeding, lethargy, vomiting, fever or low temperature, poor color

pill.text: Emergency department now: blood and urine culture, urine reducing substances, glucose, INR; neonatal or pediatric ICU if unstable

children.cond: Vomiting on milk feeds, E. coli or other gram-negative sepsis, cataracts — galactosemia possible, newborn screen pending or missing

pill.text: Send urine reducing substances now, before the switch; then stop breast milk and lactose formula — feed a soy-based or elemental formula and keep feeding; check glucose. Red-cell GALT activity (false-normal after transfusion). Mother expresses milk to keep her supply (lesson 02-03)

children.cond: Bleeding — umbilical stump, bruising, blood in stool or vomit, bulging fontanelle

pill.text: Emergency department now: vitamin K IV (slowly) now, INR, head imaging if neurologic signs — vitamin K deficiency bleeding until proved otherwise. Ask whether vitamin K was given at birth

children.cond: Visible jaundice in the first 24 hours of life

pill.text: Pathologic until proved otherwise: bilirubin now; hemolysis workup (blood groups, DAT, CBC, reticulocytes); neonatal team uses the AAP 2022 thresholds

children.h: 2 · Look at the stool and urine

children.text: Ask about stool and urine color at every visit, and look at a diaper yourself. Parents often call pale stools "yellow".

children.cond: Pale, clay-colored or white stools, or dark urine that stains the diaper — whatever the numbers

pill.text: Same-day pediatric hepatology: fractionated bilirubin and INR today — biliary atresia until proved otherwise. Look at the stool yourself

children.h: 3 · Read the direct or conjugated value

children.text: Look up every bilirubin drawn since birth. A direct or conjugated value is often reported beside the total and never read.
Read the number itself. Never divide by the total — the 20% rule misses biliary atresia.
Direct and conjugated bilirubin are different tests: direct runs higher. Know your lab's method and its upper limit.

Days 1–3: a direct (diazo) value runs higher than a conjugated one (99th centile 2.1 vs 0.5 mg/dL, Davis 2011). Still call at ≥ 1.0 mg/dL; hepatology may repeat it as conjugated within days — never wait if stools are pale (expert opinion).

children.cond: Direct or conjugated ≥ 1.0 mg/dL (17 µmol/L), at any total

pill.text: Cholestasis: call pediatric GI or hepatology today. Urinalysis and urine culture. INR — if prolonged, parenteral vitamin K and recheck INR. Do not wait for an ultrasound

children.cond: Above the lab's upper limit but below 1.0 mg/dL

pill.text: Not normal — early biliary atresia can look like this. Rule out infection (urinalysis, urine culture). Repeat total and direct (same method) by the 2-week visit; ask about stool color. Higher than before, or ≥ 1.0 mg/dL → hepatology today (expert opinion)

children.cond: Within the lab's range, or not yet measured

children.text: Total bilirubin against the AAP 2022 phototherapy and escalation thresholds for gestational age and risk factors — neonatal team.
Hemolysis (blood groups, DAT, CBC, reticulocytes, G6PD) if jaundice is early, rising fast, or near the threshold.

children.cond: Near or above the AAP 2022 phototherapy threshold, or rising fast

pill.text: Neonatal team: phototherapy per AAP 2022; hemolysis workup; feeding support

children.cond: Hemolysis, or a known unconjugated disorder in the family
Well, feeding, stools pigmented, bilirubin below threshold

pill.text: Routine newborn follow-up. Still jaundiced at 2 weeks → fractionated bilirubin (use the 2 weeks and older branch)
